lines.en: : Mr. and Mrs. Arakawa — welcome back to Chateau de L’Himawari.
: Due to recent events, our primary location is subject to temporary closure and we’ve been forced to transition to a much less glamorous building for the time being.
: Rest assured, however, our standard for quality has not changed. And we hope you’ll enjoy dining with us tonight just as much as you did last time.
: Oh no. I’m going to cry again.
: You already are.
: I can’t help it, okay?! Just a few hours ago, I wouldn’t leave the rooftop and could barely even look at her!
: But Hima-chan wasn’t offended at all and now she’s making us dinner again! She’s too good for this world! I need to starve myself to repent! I’m sorry, Hima-chan!
: Miss, I must kindly ask you to stop yelling in the restaurant. Regardless of how awestruck you are in relation to my somewhat curious existence.
: You’re going to have to kick me out then! I can’t hold it back this time!
: Are you sure this is how you want to spend your final moments, Himawari? Digging burger patties out of a McDonald’s freezer while we sit here and openly dread your imminent departure?
: Hey, you’re the ones who are going to be stuck here in an unpredictable and chaotic counterfeit world. Plus, I get to watch you whenever I want. Remember?
: Besides, you followed me around all day while I modified the brains of your loved ones in front of you. The least I can do is make you dinner.
: Mom too, of course. Because, while she didn’t help me with work, she’s earned her weight in meat after shedding more tears today than I have ever seen her cry in all my years of existence.
: I’d rather you sit here and hug me until everything is over. I won’t be able to eat right now anyway.
: I will, don’t worry. You’re not the only one dreading this. I just want our last meal together to be a happy one. And seeing as Shi-chan definitely won’t be cooking for us, that leaves me.
: I can help you. I don’t mind at all. I just...can’t guarantee that I don’t have PTSD now since the last time I cooked for you, bad things happened.
: Yeah, maybe just leave the cooking to me and keep Dad company.
: Himawari.
: Father.
: I’m sure I can speak for both of us when I say your mother and I would like to do something for you as well before we have to leave you again.
: You want to do something for me? Hurry up and uncover all the secrets of this world while I’m out on administrative leave.
: Oh, yeah. Easy. I’ll get right to that.
: Hey, I gave you a few hints. You know some of the important bits now, so you’ve just gotta run with it and hope things don’t become even more unstable.
: Oh god. That sounds like foreshadowing.
: Wish I could just confirm it. Honestly, what use is time travel at all if I can’t even see the future?
: Call it a prediction, though. Not foreshadowing. Because Maya doesn’t know she’s made-up yet. And who knows what will happen once she does?
: Which isn’t even factoring in what Ami is going to do once you tell her the charade’s over.

: You...will tell her the charade’s over, right? Because she’s your best bet at learning anything right now.  And you can’t keep letting her play house if she’s going to keep ripping the heads off of all of her dolls.
: I know. Ami’s just a little harder to parent than you are.
: Most people are, from what I understand. You guys sure lucked out, huh?
: Luck doesn’t even begin to explain it, Himawari.
: You are more than I could have ever hoped for. And it breaks my heart that you feel the need to do all of this for us when you should be living a normal life.
: So should you, though. And again, you guys have it worse than me. I can leave. I can see and experience all sorts of things and all you guys have is trapped inside this city.
: It’s fine if everything we have is locked in one place. I learned that in Aomori. And so long as I have that, I don’t need to experience anything else the world has to offer.
: I want you. And I promise — no matter which you it is, I will love you so profoundly that you will have no choice but to forget I ever doubted you at all.
: Please...find a way to come back. Because this can’t really be the end, right?
: You can’t leave now and just put fate entirely in our hands. We’ve accomplished nothing. We needed you to break the rules of the universe to just give us a hint.
: Mom, you’re forgetting one very crucial point.
: I exist because of you.
: If it weren’t for you guys, I wouldn’t be able to traverse dimensions and reveal classified info to try and steer you in the right direction.
: So all those hints are only hints at all because you were able to accomplish something amazing on your own.
: And even if it was something as simple as having a daughter and raising her with love, it ultimately led you here. It led me here.
: And it’ll surely lead us back together one day.
: I wish I could tell you when, but I can’t.
: Just know that I’ll be watching. And rooting for you to succeed where I could not.
: Now! Please excuse me while I go dig burger patties out of a McDonald’s freezer. Let’s see if I still remember how to do this.
Himawari leaves the two of us at the table, but I’m too distracted by the sound of her footsteps to think much about her speech.
Because I might never hear them again. That horrible fear that was so prevalent in my happy ending  is now my reality. Just as I knew it would be one day.
But this isn’t like I’m sending her off to college. We won’t get together for Christmas. She won’t have a family of her own.
She’ll be watching me fail from an app and bashing her head against the wall as I squander the massive opportunity she’s given me to finally do something.
She’s not even gone yet and I can already feel the old me coming back. I’m so tired of losing the people I love. Now I have to lose her? That isn’t fair.
If there are so many gods out there helping so many people, why won’t any of them save me?
Is it because I haven’t opened my heart? Is that it?

I opened it to her. I didn’t want to and I opened it to her. But I guess it was more like her carving my chest open and splitting it in two with some sort of intangible vice grip instead of a conscious decision I made.
I can’t do that for someone else. Not knowing that she is still out there.
Ayane is the same. Just like it was the first time we went out to eat with her — when we watched her gorge herself on ikura and mishandle her chopsticks and teach us what family feels like.
Neither of us will ever be the same again. We’ll never be normal again. Assuming we ever were in the first place.
But now? It’s hopeless.
How are we supposed to fly without our wings?
I think I might hate the birds too now.
I hate this world. I hate Maya for making it. I hate Ami for selfishly hiding things from me. And I hate myself for hating anything at all right now instead of using these moments for love.
And I know the fury will fade — just as Himawari will. And as I may if I can not somehow escape this fate.
All I can do is hope that the paradox of her existence proves that I’m wrong. And that one day, Ayane will get to see the look on my face when I first lay eyes on her.
That’s what I must chase now. And simply hope that I can still move forward with my kneecaps bashed in.
: Sensei?...
: Heh...
: Did you...just laugh?
: Why?
: Because you’re going back to normal too. And it took no time at all.
: Four months of “Akira” or “darling” or a million other pet names, but twelve hours back in Kumon-mi and I’m already “Sensei” again.
: Huh...
: I didn’t even realize...
: What are we going to do, Ayane?...
: Is she just always going to be in the back of our minds now? Do we have to do all of this while battling reminder after reminder of what we lost?
: Because I already see her in everything and she’s still here. And when I look at you and see her eyes, it only makes it worse.
: At least you don’t have to look in the mirror. I’m the same way, Akira. I have no idea how I’m supposed to live now.
: It’s okay if I keep calling you that, right?...
: Why wouldn’t it be?...
: Because it’s one more thing that might remind you-
: I want the reminders, though. That’s the worst fucking part. This is a loss I am afraid to suppress because it’s the first time the goods have ever outweighed the bads.
: I’m sorry...I didn’t mean to-
: Don’t apologize...
: You didn’t do anything wrong. I’m just...lashing out because I’m scared. And every minute that goes by, that fear only deepens.
: If you want a turn to vent now, go ahead. I imagine we’ll be doing a lot of that from here on out.
: I’ve already wasted too much time on misery tonight. There’s nothing I want to vent about right now other than how amazing Hima-chan is.
: Once this is over, though...and the world goes back to how it was...
: I will need to lean on you. That much I’m sure of. So please, don’t be the broken one this time.
: Ayane-
: I’m not saying you can’t be sad. I know you love her just as much as I do and that you are terrified right now. But, Akira...
: This is going to break me.
: I just...can’t do it this time.
: And honestly? I don’t think I’ll ever be the same after this.
: Not until we meet her, at least...After that, I might be able to walk on my own two feet again.
: But until that happens, please be patient with me...
: And please still love me as if I am your wife even though I won’t be...
: Of course.
: I will love you with every fiber of my being and I will carry you when you can’t walk.
: So lean on me as much you’d like. But please forgive me if my hands start to shake when I look you in the eyes.
: Because I can’t guarantee I won’t be seeing someone else sometimes.
: Awwwww! You’re so sweet when you try, Dad. I’m so proud of you.
: H-Hima-chan! How...much of that did you hear?
: Enough to know you guys are being way too sentimental for what is supposed to be a fun goodbye-dinner.
: I swear — I leave for five minutes and you guys start acting like I’m already gone. Now, move over. I’m hungry too.
: And you — stop looking so sad. Didn’t you hear that Mom’s gonna need you to man up? How are you supposed to do that with a frown that size, huh?
: I’m sorry, Himawari. It’s not every day I lose the light of my life and I’m now approaching a second instance of having to do that in less than twenty-four hours.
: Can you believe this guy? He’s got the most beautiful, most loving, and most amazing girlfriend-slash-future-wife anybody could ever want and he’s got the audacity to act gloomy. The nerve.
: Don’t pretend you aren’t proud of him, Hima-chan. He stepped up when I couldn’t. And I think that makes him pretty amazing too.
: Great. Thanks, Dad. Now I look like an asshole for trying to cheer Mom up.
: I’m claiming your second burger. I made you two because I am a good daughter, but now you can just assume I made myself two because I am a growing girl.
: Yeah...you’re going to keep growing while your mom and I are off trying to solve what all those gods can’t, aren’t you?
: I’m afraid that’s classified too, Dad.
: I feel like you’re just using the word “classified” to describe things you don’t want to tell me.
: Oh yeah? Where’s your proof?
: Don’t have any, right? That’s all speculation then. Good luck having that entered into evidence in the case of Arakawa vs Arakawa. I hope your lawyers are good.
: I’ll miss this...watching the two of you bicker with each other.
: Well, somebody’s gotta. And you two are too busy being a perfect couple to ever fight with one another. The only people willing to put him in his place are Aunt Sana and me.
: Again, please don’t take after her regarding anything ever. You are better than that and I do not want you turning into her.
: What he really means by that is he’s just worried you’ll start being interested in boys.
: Ew.
: ...Girls?
: Ew.
: Ew...to both of those things?
: That whole romance thing ain’t for me. I just want a dog.
: Are you sure you’re our daughter?
: Besides, not being interested in that stuff gives me more time to wander through time and space! Right, Dad?
: Exactly. Now please excuse me while I breathe a sigh of relief so large that I immediately suffocate and die.
: Hey, look. The frown is gone.
: You really were planning on just staying with us forever then, weren’t you?
: Mhm! You can call me a loser if you want. That’s what everybody in the office does when I tell them about my dreams.
: It doesn’t bother me, though. So a girl loves her family? Big deal. Thinking a dream like that is weird just makes me think none of those people grew up with parents half as cool as mine.
: They’re...making fun of you over there?...For just sharing your thoughts with them?
: Some people just don’t understand what ambition looks like. And that’s fine.
: Because I’ll be the one to change the world while they keep pushing papers for a soulless company that turned an amazing idea into an unorganized bureaucratic mess.
: All that matters is I have you guys. So please — make me proud. And create a world in which I can make my dreams come true.
: Or at least...the dream I have that I didn’t wind up using my wish on since it played second fiddle to an uneventful NEET life with my parents.
: So that wish thing...is really true then? That people can make worlds by just wanting them?
: Mhm. Or pint-sized nymphomaniacs in Dad’s case. But hey, to each their own.
: Have I used mine yet?
: That’s classified, Ayane.
: What a guy. You looking for a job? There might be an opening soon when a certain someone gets canned for having a heart of gold.
: I don’t think I’d get along with the gods, to be honest. But I’ll keep it in mind when I get bored from not having anyone to home-school.
: Can you really not tell me, Hima-chan?
: To be honest, I don’t know.
: You might have. And there might be a world out there where the three of us are eating at McDonald’s for real right now.
: Maybe it’s in Aomori. Maybe it’s not. And maybe it doesn’t even exist in the first place. But whatever the case, that’s not important now.
: What’s important is that this is your reality. Even if it’s just for the time being. And so this is the place where you need to try your hardest. Because that’s what life is all about, right?
: There’s a lot I still don’t know. About the world. About you guys. Myself too. But every day, I learn. And every day, I grow some more.
: The trick is following the sun. Finding the brightest star in the sky and chasing after it no matter how hot it gets.
: And sure, you might burn up before you ever get there. You probably will. But that doesn’t mean there’s not someone down below, looking up and rooting for you.
: I hate that we’re worlds apart. But there’s a certain beauty to it too, I think.
: Because we’re both chasing after the same thing. And we can both root for each other even if we can’t see one another.
: It’s like when you stare up at the sky and wonder if the person you’re thinking about is doing the same thing. Just less passive and more hopeful because there’s an ending in sight.
: And maybe we’ll wind up there at the same time one day. That, somehow, in that ever-expanding engima we call “space,” we’ll find each other at the end of our mission.
: But instead of being proud of how far we’ve come or confused about what to do next, we’ll just look at each other and smile.
: Then the camera will fade to black.
: And we will finally be able to rest.
